codeReview.summary: The multi-account callback now reuses persisted progress and resolves the first blocker, but the launcher/shutdown path still overwrites richer scrolling snapshots with coarser action metadata, so the round-3 fix does not fully clear the prior failure.

issues.description: The launcher callback now preserves persisted progress, but it still returns the coarse launcher action (`args.action`) instead of the richer scrolling action already persisted by the scrolling runtimes. For `scroll`/`reels`/`mixed`, `run_browser()` dispatches into scrolling sessions (`python/browser/runtime.py:136-141`) that save `scroll_feed` / `scroll_reels` snapshots (`python/actions/browsing/feed_scrolling/runtime.py:249`, `python/actions/browsing/reels_scrolling/runtime.py:210`). `_launcher_state_callback()` copies only the progress (`python/runners/launcher.py:189-199`), and `_run_shutdown()` only skips the write when the existing progress is strictly higher (`python/core/shutdown.py:151-164`). When the persisted progress is reused and therefore equal, shutdown still calls `save_state(profile, action, progress)` and overwrites `scroll_feed` / `scroll_reels` with the coarser launcher action, so the richer scrolling snapshot is still not preserved end-to-end.
